title: The Iron Road: Railways of Colonial India

scenes.narration_text: In 1853, the first passenger train in India left Bombay for Thane, and nothing about the subcontinent would ever move the same way again.
scenes.visual_description: Slow zoom on a vintage map of 1850s Bombay, sepia tones.

asset_requirement.description: Historical map of the Bombay region, 1850s, public domain.

scenes.narration_text: Within three decades, the network stretched from the coasts deep into the interior.
scenes.visual_description: Show archival railway footage from colonial India.

asset_requirement.description: Archival footage of Indian railways, late 19th century.

scenes.narration_text: Bridges over wide rivers became symbols of an engineering ambition that outlived the empire.
scenes.visual_description: Wide shot of a colonial-era stone railway bridge spanning a river.

asset_requirement.description: Period photograph of a stone railway bridge in India.

scenes.narration_text: For the people who built and rode these lines, the railway was neither symbol nor empire; it was daily life.
scenes.visual_description: Close, warm portrait-style still of travelers waiting on a platform.

scenes.narration_text: Today, that same iron road carries more than twenty million passengers every single day.
scenes.visual_description: Modern busy railway platform at sunrise, crowds in motion blur.

asset_requirement.description: Busy modern Indian railway platform at sunrise, crowds in motion blur.
